bridges.statement: Human persons are immaterial substantial entities—souls—that contain consciousness and animate their bodies.
Conscious mental states have properties that physical brain states lack, so consciousness is neither identical with nor reducible to the brain.
The unity, indivisibility, and persistence of persons through physical change require a substantial soul.
Free agency, rational inference, and mental causation require a nonphysical subject rather than an exclusively physical causal chain.
Brain–mind dependence and correlation do not establish mind–brain identity and are compatible with an embodied soul using the brain.
Empirical and experiential evidence, including some near-death reports, can support a cumulative case without being the primary philosophical demonstration.
No coherent, evidenced soul is needed to explain life, consciousness, cognition, or personal characteristics.
Systematic alteration of thought, memory, personality, and awareness by physical conditions supports bodily production of mind and conflicts with an independently functioning soul.
Conscious capacities occur by degrees across biological systems and emerge through continuous physical organization rather than an added immaterial entity.
A soul that interacts with bodies would have observable consequences, yet controlled inquiry has not verified such an entity.
Near-death, out-of-body, and paranormal reports are inconsistent, culturally conditioned, reproducible through brain stimulation, or otherwise insufficient evidence.
The proponent must positively define and demonstrate the proposed additional immaterial component rather than infer it merely from gaps in physical explanation.

selectionBalanceAudit.rationale: The inventory selects 42 chronologically ordered, independently assessable moves across six source-required clusters. It preserves Hernandez's philosophical case, Aron Ra's biological and empirical case, the distinction between dependence evidence and deductive identity, the gap between criticizing reductive physicalism and positively demonstrating a soul, and explicit concessions about brain effects, free-will uncertainty, neurological expertise, and the limited role of near-death evidence. Moderator material, personal invective, extended theology, and repeated summaries were excluded unless a substantive answer directly bore on the soul motion. A score-blind capacity check then separated the biological-continuity cluster and reassigned the report-consistency and culturally conditioned-content objections to their closest existing methodological and mental-content sections, preserving all 42 moves while bringing every side of every section to four cards or fewer. The independent source audit found con-16 and con-21 substantively duplicative; con-16 was removed before judgment, and every remaining audit-directed proposition or source-span correction was applied. Several proposed auditor spans still exceeded the frozen transport limits, so their endpoints were tightened deterministically within the same speaker turns while preserving the auditor's narrowed inference.
